_doc: GOALS-1 (Rowan, 2026-11-18): "What are you working toward? What is your target? You have to set your own goals ... with knobs that it can fiddle to reach those goals." A goal tree from the standing goal (bootstrap to criticality) down to small goals, in Ashby's terms (ULTRASTABILITY-1): each goal is an essential variable with a measured reading, a bound and a deadline, plus the knobs the system may turn to bring it back. foundation/goals.py reads every variable from live ledgers, and when a goal stays out of bounds for patience_ticks it turns one knob one step inside the knob's safe range, logs the step as a decision with a prediction (decision point goal-knob), keeps it only if the variable moves toward its target within settle_ticks, and otherwise restores it. When every knob is spent and the goal is still missed it re-plans: a Q-GOAL-<id>-REPLAN item and a proposal row name the new knob or sub-goal. The system also revises and adds goals itself (ratchet after a met streak; generators from the idea loop), each with a provenance row. A bound is a viability limit: never edit a target to clear a miss, change it by a PR with a lineage note. Every goal has a measured variable and at least one knob (doctrine/rules.json rule every-goal-has-knob). Read by foundation/goals.py; checked by `python3 -m foundation goals --check`; served at /goals and /api/goals from site/goals-data.js (generated).

knobs.what: how many times a day the executor may wake itself (loop interval)
spinoff cap per day: how many new public apps the loop may launch in a day (the free-tier governor still sheds below it)
the idea loop's score floor: lower queues more ideas, higher queues fewer
how many new ideas one idea-loop run may queue
the protected plussing budget share: capacity reserved for improvements so work does not collapse into bug fixes

goals.name: Bootstrap to criticality: a self-sustaining Ultrastable
goals.why: The standing goal (Rowan, 2026-11-13): the system deploys its own workers and every verified deploy it makes pays for the next, with no hand-holding.
goals.how: Met when its children are met; the regime is read from foundation/criticality.py.

goals.name: Deploys the system originates and ships itself
goals.why: Proof signal 1 of criticality: a rising count of verified deploys that no outside session drove (k_self).

goals.name: Spend stays under budget
goals.why: Proof signal 2 of criticality: spend stays inside the free-plan budget, and a paid plan needs a measured return first.
goals.integrates: infrastructure-boundary optimizer: its interval stretch is registered here as one more knob when it lands (doctrine/knobs entries are never duplicated)

goals.name: Autonomy rate: work with no person in the path
goals.why: Headline metric of the guiding directive: autonomous steps over autonomous steps plus human touches.

goals.name: Public-benefit apps launched and really used
goals.why: Blue sky: the system makes things strangers use. An app counts when its own first-party metrics show a use in the last 7 days.
goals.unit: apps with at least one use in 7 days

goals.name: Queued app ideas become launched apps
goals.why: An idea that sits queued is a loop that does not close; the idea loop's output must have a consumer.

goals.name: Tenants served, all on the free plan
goals.why: Blue sky: Ultrastable runs other people's systems, not only its own, and the demo stays inside the free plan.
goals.note: Only one knob moves tenant work today; when it is spent the engine files a re-plan for a tenant-intake knob.

goals.name: Free-plan headroom stays available
goals.why: The free tier is a ceiling: the busiest resource is held below the target share of its daily limit so nothing sheds.

goals.name: Every public statement matches the code
goals.why: Small goal mirrored from an essential variable: words that no longer match code break the system's record of itself.

goals.name: Deploys are verified live
goals.why: Small goal mirrored from an essential variable: a deploy whose live code differs from its commit means the shipping loop is not closing.

generators.what: when the idea loop queues more than the threshold the system adds a queue-depth goal with its knobs (already adopted as idea-queue-drained)
